title: Family and friends
subtitle: widow, stepfather, twins, mate
summary: Talk about your relatives and your friends - a widow, a stepfather, twins, in-laws, mates and ex-girlfriends.

lesson.heading: Relatives
lesson.text: Your **relatives** are the members of your family. **Relations** means exactly the same thing. Here a young man from Germany describes his family.

examples.text: My father died when I was nine, so my mother was a **widow** with four young children.
examples.note: a widow = a woman whose husband has died

examples.text: She **remarried** five years later, so now I have a **stepfather**.
examples.note: remarry = get married again; a stepfather is the man married to your mother who is not your real father

examples.text: I've got an **elder** brother called Thomas.
My two younger sisters, Anya and Claudia, are **twins**.
examples.note: twins = two children born to one mother at the same time

lesson.heading: Close families and only children
lesson.text: A **close family** is a family whose members like each other and spend a lot of time together. A person with no brothers or sisters is an **only child**. If you have a good relationship with someone, you **get on well with** them.

examples.text: My mother is an **only child**, but I've got two uncles on my father's side.
I **get on well with** Uncle Rolf, and he always tells me I'm his favourite nephew.

lesson.heading: Family words you may not know
rows: a woman whose husband has died
the man married to your mother who is not your real father
two children born to one mother at the same time
a person with no brothers or sisters
your brother's wife, or your husband's or wife's sister
your sister's husband, or your husband's or wife's brother
lesson.note: We also say mother-in-law, father-in-law, son-in-law and daughter-in-law.

lesson.text: It is more common and more natural to say *Thomas's wife* and *Anna's younger sister*, not ~~the wife of Thomas~~ or ~~the younger sister of Anna~~.

lesson.heading: Friends
lesson.text: A person you were at school with is an **old school friend**. When you meet someone and slowly become friends, you **get to know** each other. **Mate** is an informal word for a friend, and the noun for two people being friends is **friendship**.

examples.text: My best friend is Florian, an old **school friend**.
We **got to know** each other when we were in the same class at school.

examples.note: ever since = from that time until now

examples.text: Our **friendship** is very important to both of us.

lesson.heading: current and ex-
lesson.text: Your **current** girlfriend or boyfriend is the one you have now. We use the prefix **ex-** for a relationship we had in the past but do not have now.

examples.text: His **current** girlfriend is actually one of Thomas's **ex-girlfriends**.
The children stay with my **ex-husband** at the weekend.
I saw an **ex-girlfriend** of mine yesterday.

lesson.note: It is nice if you can still get on well with an ex-boyfriend or ex-girlfriend.

exercises.prompt: Cath's husband Simon died two years ago, so Cath is a ___.
exercises.explanation: A woman whose husband has died is a widow.

exercises.prompt: Emily has no brothers or sisters, so she is an ___ child.
exercises.explanation: A child with no brothers or sisters is an only child.

exercises.prompt: Cath and Brian are brother and sister. Brian's daughter is Leyla. What is Leyla to Cath?
exercises.explanation: Your brother's daughter is your niece.
Your brother's son is your nephew.

exercises.prompt: Emily is Cath's daughter and Leyla is Brian's daughter, so Emily is Leyla's ___.
exercises.hint: (the same word for a boy or a girl)
exercises.explanation: The children of your aunt or uncle are your cousins.

exercises.prompt: Tom is 16 and his sister Leyla is 14, so Tom is Leyla's ___ brother.
Brian is married to Meg, and Cath is Brian's sister. What is Cath to Meg?
exercises.explanation: Your husband's sister is your sister-in-law.

exercises.prompt: Match each explanation with the word it defines.

pairs.left: all the members of your family
the friend you like more than any other
someone you have known for a long time
two children born to one mother at the same time
an informal word for a friend

exercises.prompt: It's nice if you can still ___ with an ex-boyfriend or ex-girlfriend.
exercises.hint: (two or three words: have a good relationship)
exercises.explanation: get on (well) with someone = have a good relationship with them.

exercises.prompt: Is the word about family or about friends?
We got married three years ago, and we've been going to the same gym ever ___ we got married.
exercises.explanation: ever since = from that time until now.

exercises.statement: In natural English we normally say 'the wife of Thomas' rather than 'Thomas's wife'.
exercises.explanation: It is more common and more natural to say 'Thomas's wife'.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say how two friends became friends.
exercises.answer: We got to know each other at school.
exercises.explanation: get to know someone = slowly become friends with them.
